title: DR1 asks for each animal's permanent address on its own page among the consignment parties; the frontend asks it inside the identification entry form, one animal at a time

controls.text: Where will their permanent address be?

finding.frontend: The frontend does ask the question. It renders a "Permanent address" heading, the sentence "A permanent address is required for this animal." and a full address form inside the identification card, below the identifier boxes and above the save button — src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/animal-identification/_identification-card.njk:43-69, gated on the card's showAddress flag. The gate is the permanentAddress obligation in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js:200-208, allow-listed to Cat and Dog in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/services/commodities/stub.js:115. So the user meets the question once per animal, interleaved with that animal's identifiers, and answers it as many times as there are animals on the line. No frontend capture shows it: the corpus photographed cow, horse and fish, none of which is on the allow list.
finding.prototype: DR1 gives it a page of its own, /permanent-address/select, headed "Permanent address" under the "Consignment parties" caption, reached from the roles-and-addresses list as a section beside consignor, consignee, importer and place of destination — app/data/consignment-address-sections.js:79-97 declares it, and :124-131 attaches it to commodity code 01061900, where it stands in place of the CPH row that cattle and pig notifications get, so that list is still six rows long. The page asks about every animal at once: one bordered card per animal, headed "Canis familiaris 1", "Canis familiaris 2", each card repeating that animal's already-entered identifiers in an inset so the user can tell them apart (app/views/permanent-address-animals.html:66-97), and one set of page-level Save and continue / Save and return buttons at the foot. The dr1-permanent-address-animals capture shows two dog cards on one page. DR1 asks the question for cat, dog and ferret, one commodity more than the frontend's two.
finding.difference: Move the question out of the identification card and onto a page of its own in the addresses part of the journey, listing every animal on every permanent-address commodity line at once. That means: a new page and route; a section row alongside the other consignment-party addresses, standing where the CPH row does on a cattle notification rather than beside it; removing the showAddress branch from _identification-card.njk:43-69 and the address fields from the identification card view model; and re-pointing the stored answer, which today hangs off the animal record as `permanentAddress` inside animalIdentifiers. The per-animal granularity does not change — DR1 asks per animal too — only where and how many at a time. Because the new page needs the animals to exist first, it has to sit after identification in the flow even though it belongs with the addresses; check the ordering against the hub task rows before building. Who the rule applies to is not part of this change: DR1's set is cat, dog and ferret against the frontend's cat and dog, and ferret is not in the frontend's commodity catalogue at all, so the allow list widens when the catalogue does and the catalogue finding already carries that dependency by name.
finding.falsifiedBy: Rendering the frontend identification page for a Cat or Dog line and finding no Permanent address block inside the card, or finding a standalone frontend permanent-address route.
finding.verification: The load-bearing check on this slice, because no capture in this corpus shows the frontend's permanent-address block at all, so the whole claim rests on establishing what actually renders, for which commodities, under what gate. Traced it end to end. _identification-card.njk:43-69 emits an h3 from copy.permanentAddress.heading, a paragraph from copy.permanentAddress.required (copy.en.js:90-93, "Permanent address" and "A permanent address is required for this animal.") and then card.addressFields, inside the not-at-maximum branch and above the in-card button. card.showAddress is set in card/view-model.js:92 and :110 from permanentAddressApplies, which is appliesForCommodity('permanentAddress', commodity) at identifier/fields.js:32-33; that reads the obligation manifest's gate metadata (bridge/applicability.js:29-34), and for this obligation the gate is allowListed(commodityCode, permanentAddressCommodities, unitRecord) at identifiers.js:200-207 over PERMANENT_ADDRESS_COMMODITIES = ['Cat', 'Dog'] at stub.js:115. Cat and Dog are real picker options (stub.js:1). addressFieldsFor at address/fields.js:117-163 returns the nine controls in the order given. Two of the repo's own tests pin the render rather than the wiring: the identifier render matrix at animal-identification.controller.test.js:364-406 asserts showAddress true for Cat and Dog and false for Cow, Horse and Fish; and the browser fit spec at journeys/linear/features/commodities/fit/identification.fit.spec.js opens a Cat line, fills #nameOrOrganisationName-0 through #emailAddress-0 including the country select, saves, and reads the permanent-address name back off the saved row. So the block renders, inline in the card, once per animal, for Cat and Dog only, and the author's account is right. Opened dr1-permanent-address-animals, screenshot and rendered DOM, for the other side: /permanent-address/select, caption "Consignment parties", two Canis familiaris cards on one page, one set of page-level buttons. CORRECT.
finding.correction: One citation was wrong and is fixed in place. The commodity attachment was given as app/data/consignment-address-sections.js:113-130, which lands on the 0103 block; the 01061900 list that carries 'permanent-address' is :124-131. The section declaration is :79-97, given as :79-96. The claim itself is right at the corrected lines. Two things the finding asserts are not visible in any capture and it did not say so. DR1's permanent-address row in the roles-and-addresses list is unphotographed — the three dr1-roles-and-addresses captures are a cattle notification, and the string "permanent address" appears in no prototype capture but dr1-permanent-address-animals. And the identifier inset inside each DR1 card (permanent-address-animals.html:72-80) renders only when that animal already has identifiers, which the captured session did not, so the picture shows bare cards. Two further things were established when the question of who the rule applies to was put to this finding, and both are now in the prose. First, the row is not a seventh section: for 01061900 the section list is place of origin, consignor or exporter, consignee, importer, place of destination and permanent address, exactly six, standing where 0102 and 0103 put the CPH row (app/data/consignment-address-sections.js:108-131). Second, DR1's scope is cat, dog and ferret and nothing wider. requiresPermanentAddress is set on those three commodities alone (app/data/commodities.js:150, :170 and :190) and deliberately not on "Other live mammals", which shares the code 01061900 (:206-222); the code-based attachment does not sweep it in, because getSessionConsignmentAddressSections filters the row back out unless a selected species carries the flag (app/routes.js:2036-2038, over isPermanentAddressSpecies at :2016-2020), and buildPermanentAddressAnimalList skips those species when building the cards (:2357-2360). So the only residual scope difference is ferret, ferret is absent from the frontend's catalogue entirely, and commodities--commodity-catalogue already names the permanent-address list as one of the allow lists that has to gain it. No separate finding is raised for the scope, because it would be that finding a second time.

relatedTo.why: DR1 asks the permanent-address question for ferret as well as cat and dog; ferret is not in the frontend's catalogue, so the allow list widens only when the catalogue does, and that finding already carries the dependency
